issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no hard-coded answers. Test labels are never used: only Xtr and y go into fitting, and Xte is used only for predict.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. All randomness comes from the seed argument (seed + 1000*k). The Ridge part does not depend on the seed, so it is computed once and reused in each of the 3 blends, which is correct. Averaging the rank-normalised blends keeps the output at one number per test molecule.
Recomputed z: (0.4745 - 0.4743) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) = 0.0002 / 0.0099 ≈ 0.020, which matches the harness. The gain is about 0.03 noise sd, so it is not detectable.

This is a non-veto concern. The change roughly triples the cost of fitting the tree models (9 fits per fold instead of 3), which brings the job closer to the 10-minute limit. It also adds code for no measurable gain. Under the 'simpler is better' rule, the provisional reject is appropriate.
